notes.text: The word — Or, the matter or thing, as this Hebrew word commonly signifies; the prophecy or vision.

In the last days — In the times of the Messiah. For Christ's institutions were to continue to the end of the world. The mountain - The temple of the Lord which is upon mount Moriah; which yet is not to be understood literally of that material temple, but mystically of the church of God; as appears from the flowing of all nations to it, which was not to that temple, nor indeed was fulfilled 'till that temple was destroyed. Exalted - Shall be placed and settled in a most conspicuous and glorious manner, being advanced above all other churches and kingdoms.

The law — The new law, the doctrine of the gospel, which is frequently called a law, because it hath the nature and power of a law, obliging us no less to the belief and practice of it, than the old law did.

He — Christ shall set up his authority among all nations, not only giving laws to them, but doing what no other can do, convincing their consciences, changing their hearts, and ordering their lives. Rebuke - By his word and Spirit, convincing the world of sin; and by his judgments upon his implacable enemies, which obstruct the propagation of the gospel.
The light — Take heed that you do not reject that light which is so clear that even the blind Gentiles will discern it.

glossa.text:
*In the last days.* ((HIER.)) Of which Jacob, etc., *as far as: it grew into a great mountain.*

*A mountain. Mountains,* the angels, the prophets, the patriarchs, the apostles, the martyrs, and the rest who shone forth with miracles. *Hills,* the lesser, receiving their light from the greater.

*And it shall be exalted.* ((ID.)) Above all the saints, because of his fulness all receive (of whom: *The mountains round about it* ), who are called mountains from Christ the mountain.

*The house.* ((ID.)) Which is said for this reason, that we may receive the Old Testament, and may not, after Manichaeus, seek another house than the house of the God of Jacob.

 *His ways,* which others have trodden. The Lord too, going up into the mountain, taught his disciples. First, then, the ways must be learned; afterward one must walk in the paths.

*Out of Sion.* ((HIER.)) Not from the rock Sina, but from mount Sion, in which is Jerusalem, in which is the temple and the religion of God. The Lord also taught in the temple, because it was not fitting that a Prophet should die outside Jerusalem.

*The law and the word.* As above, he set the word and the law together, so that the princes might hear the word, and the people take in the law with the ear. For he who shall have kept the law will come through to the word of God; the law will go forth from the word as from a fountain, that it may water others.
*And they shall stand fast their swords.* ((ID.)) All zeal for warring shall be turned into peace, etc., *as far as* let us eat at the time of harvest, that is, of death.

*O house of Jacob,* etc. ((ID.)) After the calling of the nations and the showing of the mountain of God, he invites his own people, who are of Jacob, that, going out from the darkness of unbelief, they may receive the light of Christ.

*In the light.* ((ID.)) *Whilst you have the light, believe in the light. Come ye to him and be enlightened,* etc. As if he shall say: *He that doth evil hateth the light: but come with me, let us walk in the light of the Lord, who saith: I am the light of the world,* etc.

notes.text: The tribes — Whom God has chosen to be his people. Unto - Unto the ark, called the testimony, because of the tables of the covenant laid up in it, which are called God's testimony, and the tables of the testimony. And this is called the testimony of, or to Israel, because it was given by God to them. Give thanks - To worship God; this one eminent part thereof being put for all the rest.

Judgment — The supreme courts of justice for ecclesiastical and civil affairs. Thrones - The royal throne allotted by God to David and to his posterity, and the inferior seats of justice under his authority. The psalmist expresses and prays for deliverance from trouble, ver. 1-4. A song of degrees.

glossa.text:
*A canticle of degrees.* ((CASS.)) The third degree. A great joy: to be conversant in the Church with a pure mind, and worthily to serve God as a soldier in this pilgrimage: whence we sigh for the heavenly Jerusalem, to which we are lifted by the two wings of love.

*I rejoiced at these things,* etc. First he rejoices that he has been admonished to go to Jerusalem, where the saints, secure, shall judge him *eum*; read *cum*, "with" with the Lord. Secondly, being about to ascend, he wishes for an abundance of peace: *Pray ye for the things that are for the peace,* etc.

*A testimony to Israel.* ((AUG.)) That is, in whom it is known that they are truly Israel. For when the grains are with the chaff, the whole is thought to be chaff; but when they shall be separated, then shall there be a testimony to Israel.
*Seats.* ((ID.)) That is, the just, in whom God *Deum*; read *Deus*, "God sits" sits, etc., *as far as* let all therefore who are to be questioned beware for themselves.

*Pray ye.* ((CASS.)) The second part, where he speaks to the judges, wishing them the abundance of peace which he proclaimed out of love of the brethren. *To them that love.* ((AUG.)) He who loves in another the good which he himself cannot have, it is reckoned to him as though he had it; whence: If charity has not what to give, let it give a cup of water; and as much is reckoned to him as to Zacchaeus his many gifts ((Matth. X)). The means are unequal, but the charity is not unequal.

*Let peace be made.* ((ID.)) Charity is a virtue strong as death, etc., *as far as* he subjoins: *Because of my brethren.*

*In the towers.* ((ID.)) That is, in thy high places. The judges are few, but many shall pertain to each one of them, whom they shall receive into everlasting tabernacles, and then shall there be *abundance in the towers;* but God is their whole abundance, both of those who receive and of those who are received.

*Because of the house of the Lord God.* Or thou mayest so read it that this verse is the exposition of the preceding. As it were, *I spoke peace of thee, for neighbours, brethren,* namely: *I have sought good things for thee, because of the house of the Lord our God.* The sense of these words is not changed. *For thee.* O thou, heavenly Jerusalem, because thou art the house of God, and so in this hoc, that I love thee, I love God.

notes.text: And do this — Fulfil the law of love in all the instances above mentioned. Knowing the season - Full of grace, but hasting away. That it is high time to awake out of sleep - How beautifully is the metaphor carried on! This life, a night; the resurrection, the day; the gospel shining on the heart, the dawn of this day; we are to awake out of sleep; to rise up and throw away our night-clothes, fit only for darkness, and put on new; and, being soldiers, we are to arm, and prepare for fight, who are encompassed with so many enemies. The day dawns when we receive faith, and then sleep gives place. Then it is time to rise, to arm, to walk, to work, lest sleep steal upon us again. Final salvation, glory, is nearer to us now, than when we first believed - It is continually advancing, flying forward upon the swiftest wings of time. And that which remains between the present hour and eternity is comparatively but a moment.

But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ — Herein is contained the whole of our salvation. It is a strong and beautiful expression for the most intimate union with him, and being clothed with all the graces which were in him. The apostle does not say, Put on purity and sobriety, peacefulness and benevolence; but he says all this and a thousand times more at once, in saying, Put on Christ. And make not provision - To raise foolish desires, or, when they are raised already, to satisfy them.

glossa.text: *And this knowing.* Namely, that it is the hour; or, as certain books have it: knowing this time, namely of grace. Now from the time when we have had love; it is the hour, that is, the opportunity, but a brief one. *To rise from sleep.* Sleep is negligence or ignorance. *For now.* Causes interposed, why we ought to rise. *Is nearer.* He that works well is near to eternal life. For baptism is unto pardon, a good life unto the crown. Or *nearer*, because we are more nigh to death.

*The night is past.* Again it is shown why they ought to rise: because the *night* of unbelief and ignorance *is past*, that is, has been; but now it is not, whose memory admonishes, that ye may beware. *But the day*, that is, eternal blessedness, *is at hand*, since sins are remitted, since ye are just through grace. The *night* is the old man, who passed away in baptism; the *day* is Christ the sun of justice, by whose light they have learned the truth, that they may know what is to be done. *The works of darkness.* Evil works, which have come out of the darkness of ignorance, or love the darkness, and lead to the darkness

*Not in rioting.* Note that in these things the Romans are touched; and therefore they have no right of boasting.

((AUG.)) But of these diseases pride is the mother, and the greediness of the human mind, which also often begets hypocrisy; this is not resisted, unless by frequent testimonies of the divine books fear and charity be struck in.

notes.text: But of that day — The day of judgment; Knoweth no man - Not while our Lord was on earth. Yet it might be afterward revealed to St. John consistently with this.
One is taken — Into God's immediate protection: and one is left - To share the common calamities. Our Lord speaks as having the whole transaction present before his eyes.
Two women shall be grinding — Which was then a common employment of women.
Ye know not what hour your Lord cometh — Either to require your soul of you, or to avenge himself of this nation. Mark xiii, 33; Luke xii, 35; xxi, 34.

glossa.text: *Of the day.* Lest perhaps, when the signs had been heard, they should seek also the fixed limit of that day, he says: Of the last day, after how many years or days it is to come, be not solicitous, it has been defined to no one whether the judgment shall be by day or by night, but the day is spoken of for manifestation, or the night for concealment. *No one knows,* etc. In certain codices there is added, *neither the Son.* Who indeed knows all things with the Father, but does not make men know, as the Apostle says: *That in him are hidden the treasures of wisdom and of knowledge ((II Col. II))*. He does not make it known, because it would be known to no profit. But let us always be uncertain of the coming of the judge, that we may so live every day as though we were to be judged on the next. Nor have the elect angels made anyone know it. Or God has granted the knowledge of this day to none of the holy angels, nor to an adopted son, that is, nor to any of holy men.

*But as.* He affirms the suddenness of the day of his coming by very many examples: for he both compared it to the lightning that flies swiftly over all things, and likens it to the days of Noe, or of Lot according to another evangelist.

*Eating and drinking, marrying,* etc. Not foods and marriages, but the immoderate use of lawful things is reproved. After wars, famines, earthquakes, etc., then a short peace shall follow, that the believer may be tried, whether, when the evils are past, he hopes that the judge will come, whence it is said: *For when they shall say peace and security, then shall sudden destruction come upon them ((I Thess. V))*.

*Then,* etc. Luke, *in that night,* that is, in that tribulation in which they are tried, in which some stand fast, others fall. *Two shall be.* There are two sorts of the aforesaid in the Church, of those labouring as it were in a field, of those who sincerely announce Christ, and of those who adulterate the word of God.

*Two grinding.* Two sorts of those who follow the round of changeable things, who are designated by the feminine gender, because women are governed by men, by the counsel of their betters. *Two in a bed.* Those who choose leisure and rest, which are signified by the name of the bed, occupied neither with secular nor with ecclesiastical business. *One shall be taken.* He who for God's sake strives to be continent, that living without solicitude he may think on the things that are God's. But he who has chosen the monastic life for human praise or through some corruption of vices, shall be left by God. There are no other kinds of men in the Church than these three. Whence Ezechiel saw three men delivered, Noe, Daniel and Job, that is, rulers like Noe, the continent like Daniel, the married like Job. And according to these three kinds of men he sets down three parables. In the first he treats of those labouring in the field, which is where he says: *Watch ye therefore.* In the second he treats of those who are in the bed, which is where he says: *The kingdom of heaven is like to ten virgins.* In the third he treats of those grinding at the mill, which is where he says: *For even as a man going into a far country,* etc.
*Watch ye therefore. ((HIER.))* He did not say, because we know not, but, because you know not, that he might show that he himself is not ignorant of the day of judgment.

*If he knew,* etc. The thief breaks through the house while the father of the household knows it not, because while the spirit sleeps from its own guarding, unforeseen death bursts into the dwelling of the flesh, and drags it away to punishment. But he would withstand the thief if he watched, because, guarding beforehand against the coming of the judge who comes secretly, he would meet him by doing penance.

echoes.text: He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head; and he put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a mantle.
echoes.note: 'He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head' — the divine-warrior imagery of donning protective armor underlies 'put on the armor of light' (v.12) and 'put on the Lord Jesus Christ' (v.14). Paul develops this same Isaianic armor motif at Ephesians 6 and 1 Thessalonians 5:8.

echoes.text: He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, And will array himself with judgement unfeigned as with a helmet; He will take holiness as an invincible shield,
echoes.note: 'He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and wear impartial justice as a helmet' — this Second Temple reworking of Isaiah 59:17 stands in the same stream feeding Paul's 'put on the armor of light' (v.12).

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you. Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
echoes.note: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come... darkness shall cover the earth... but the LORD will arise upon you' — the dawning of eschatological light dispelling darkness parallels 'the night is far gone, the day is near' and the light/darkness antithesis of vv.12-13.

echoes.text: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion; put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.
echoes.note: 'Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion; put on your beautiful garments' — combines the summons to wake and the imperative to 'put on,' both present in Paul's 'awaken out of sleep' (v.11) and 'put on the armor of light' / 'put on the Lord Jesus Christ' (vv.12,14).

echoes.text: Awake, awake, stand up, Jerusalem, that have drunk at the hand of Yahweh the cup of his wrath; you have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.
echoes.note: 'Rouse yourself, rouse yourself, stand up, O Jerusalem' — the prophetic call to awaken to the hour of salvation parallels 'it is already time for you to awaken out of sleep' (v.11).

echoes.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
echoes.note: 'The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light' — the night-to-day, darkness-to-light reversal of vv.12-13 resonates with this classic salvation-light oracle.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: 'He has clothed me with the garments of salvation... as a bridegroom decks himself' — the salvific 'putting on' of clothing as a figure for new status anticipates 'put on the Lord Jesus Christ' (v.14).

echoes.text: But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out, and leap like calves of the stall.
echoes.note: 'The sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings' — the dawning day of salvation coheres with 'the day is near' (v.12) and the nearness of salvation (v.11).

echoes.text: Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.
echoes.note: 'Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust' — eschatological awakening from sleep/death as a figure of salvation faintly parallels 'awaken out of sleep' (v.11).

echoes.text: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths. The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief. The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye shall see me.’ He disguises his face. In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light. For the morning is to all of them like thick […]
echoes.note: Those who 'rebel against the light' and work evil under cover of night/darkness anticipate 'the works of darkness' (v.12) contrasted with walking properly 'as in the day' (v.13).

echoes.text: Don’t be among ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat: for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
echoes.note: 'Be not among drunkards... for the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty' — sapiential warning against carousing and drunkenness behind 'not in reveling and drunkenness' (v.13).

echoes.text: Woe to those who rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; who stay late into the night, until wine inflames them!
echoes.note: Woe to those who 'run after strong drink... till wine inflames them' — prophetic censure of revelry and drunkenness parallels the vice-list of v.13.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Noah went into the ship with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives, because of the floodwaters.
echoes.note: 'As the days of Noah were... eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and they didn't know until the flood came and took them all away' is a sustained allusion to Genesis 6-7, the flood narrative; the unsuspecting world swept away while Noah enters the ark is the controlling typology.

echoes.text: Every living thing was destroyed that was on the surface of the ground, including man, livestock, creeping things, and birds of the sky. They were destroyed from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those who were with him in the ship.
echoes.note: The flood that 'took them all away' (every living thing blotted out, only Noah and those with him remaining, Gen 7:23) is the precise source for the sudden, total, unexpected sweeping-away that figures the Son of Man's coming.

echoes.text: Yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.
echoes.note: The heedless eating, drinking, and marrying corresponds to the corrupt complacency of Noah's generation (Gen 6:5,11-12), heightening the contrast with the abrupt judgment.

echoes.text: In the same day Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japheth—the sons of Noah—and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered into the ship—
echoes.note: 'the day that Noah entered the ark' (Gen 7:13) marks the decisive divide between the saved and the swept-away that the parable applies to the day of the Son of Man.

echoes.text: I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it shall be for a time, times, and a half; and when they have made an end of breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.
echoes.note: The withholding of the precise time even from heavenly beings, known only to God, resonates with Daniel sealing the appointed time until the end, knowledge reserved to God alone.

echoes.text: It will be a unique day which is known to Yahweh; not day, and not night; but it will come to pass, that at evening time there will be light.
echoes.note: 'a day known to the LORD' alone (Zech 14:7) parallels 'no one knows of that day and hour... but my Father only,' the day's timing reserved to God.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: The sudden, unanticipated arrival of the Lord who 'will suddenly come to his temple' (Mal 3:1) resonates with the Lord coming at an unexpected hour for which one must be ready.

echoes.text: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? if thieves by night, wouldn’t they destroy until they had enough?
echoes.note: The thief-in-the-night image of unexpected nocturnal plunder (cf. Jer 49:9; Obad 5, thieves who take only what they want by night) supplies the figure of the thief whose hour the householder cannot predict.

echoes.text: The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.
echoes.note: The thief/murderer who rises in the dark and breaks into houses (Job 24:14,16) furnishes the burglary imagery for the unexpected coming for which one must keep watch.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The night is far gone, the day is near.
Wake from sleep; the Lord is coming.
Let us go up to the house of the Lord.
We will walk in the light of God.
Keep watch, for we do not know the hour.
We are watching. We are ready.
Come, let us worship the God who comes.
Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The sky is still dark, but there is a thin line of grey at its edge — morning is coming, and we have been awake all night, waiting.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Lay down the weapons you carry, the old quarrels, the heavy night — the prophet says the swords will be hammered into plows.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Come up the mountain road with us, into the house of the Lord, where the light is already on.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Keep awake, friends; the One we have waited for is nearer now than when we began.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The night is nearly over; the day is at the door.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Wake from sleep and walk in the light.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Keep watch for the hour we cannot name.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Come, let us worship the God who is near.
